questions.q: Under what name did Bitcoin's anonymous creator release the digital currency in 2009?
a: Satoshi Nakamoto
Nathaniel Popper
Hal Finney
Ross Ulbricht
questions.why: Lesson 1 says an anonymous user called Satoshi Nakamoto introduced Bitcoin in January 2009.

questions.q: What does the summary say the blockchain is?
a: A public database of every Bitcoin transaction
A private ledger held by the largest banks
A security chip inside each Bitcoin wallet
A fund that stabilises the price of Bitcoin
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the blockchain as a communal database anyone can inspect, showing every transaction.

questions.q: Why did Bitcoin appeal to people during Argentina's financial crisis?
a: It shielded their savings from government interference and inflation
It was officially backed by the Argentine government
It paid interest that beat local bank accounts
It let them avoid paying any taxes on purchases
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that Bitcoin sidestepped government controls and protected funds while the peso lost value.

questions.q: Which advantage does the summary highlight for Bitcoin over ordinary bank transfers?
a: Money can be sent almost instantly
Transfers are insured by the government
Transfers can be reversed on request
Banks must approve every transaction
questions.why: Lesson 3 points out that bank transfers still take days while Bitcoin moves money immediately.

questions.q: What does Bitcoin's ability to be split into tiny amounts make possible?
a: Very small payments for online services
Loans without any collateral
Interest on unused wallets
Free international bank transfers
questions.why: Lesson 3 says divisibility allows microtransactions, such as paying a fraction of a cent to skip an ad.
